fatal_errors: The hypothesis replaces the target deionized-water temperature study with an ambient 3.5 wt.% NaCl experiment, changing the controlling chemistry and omitting the key 25–100 °C variable.
It omits the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 versus identically conditioned duplex stainless steel 2205 comparison and the three-cycle approximately 1100 °C thermal-shock intervention.
It does not predict the central nonmonotonic result: minimum degradation near 50 °C, with abrasion at 25 °C and unstable oxide or tribo-layer disruption at 100 °C.
It does not address retention of the HEA L12/B2 lamellar structure versus major gamma-to-delta redistribution in DS2205.
The proposed film-enhancement treatment may alter microstructure, hardness, residual stress, and composition, so it does not cleanly isolate passive-film stability.
explanation: The response captures one real part of the target mechanism: sliding-induced passive-film rupture, exposed-metal corrosion, repassivation, and feedback of corrosion products on friction and wear. Its OCP-based test and explicit falsification rule are directionally appropriate, and E1 directly supports using OCP changes to track depassivation and post-sliding repassivation. However, it remains a generic tribocorrosion hypothesis rather than a reconstruction of the study. It misses the specific alloy, dual-phase structural mediator, DS2205 comparator, thermal-shock conditioning, deionized-water environment, temperature-dependent transition among abrasion, polishing, and third-body or oxidative wear, and the order-of-magnitude performance advantage of the HEA. The inert-wear and static-corrosion baselines can estimate synergy but do not supply the matched material comparison requested. Evidence E3 supports generic erosion-corrosion synergy but is not equivalent to reciprocating tribocorrosion, while E2 is only indirect support for oxide protection. Thus the core film-rupture concept partially agrees, but the governing temperature–film-stability competition and principal outcomes are not recovered.
